description: A single-panel plot with no panel letters and no legend box, carrying two curves that share one ordinate. The abscissa is labelled "True strain" and runs 0 to 0.8 with major ticks every 0.2; the shared ordinate is labelled "Strain hardening rate, or True stress (MPa)" and runs 0 to 2500 with major ticks every 500. A red curve, identified by an arrowed text label "True stress-true strain", starts near 500 MPa at the smallest strains, rises almost linearly past 1500 MPa near strain 0.6, peaks just above 1600 MPa between strain 0.6 and 0.7, then falls steeply to roughly 1200 MPa. A blue curve, arrowed and labelled "Strain hardening rate", starts near the top of the axis (close to 2500 MPa) at the lowest strain, plunges to a minimum around 1550 MPa below strain 0.1, climbs to a broad local maximum just under 1900 MPa near strain 0.45-0.55, then declines and finally drops sharply. The composition "Fe-28Mn-9Al-0.8C" is printed in the lower-right corner. No data labels, error bars, insets, micrographs or scale bars appear; all values must be bracketed against the gridlines. The panel shows the coexistence of a rising true-stress curve with a sustained high strain-hardening rate.

observations.observation: The figure is a single panel with two curves on a shared ordinate axis labelled "Strain hardening rate, or True stress (MPa)", scaled 0 to 2500 with major ticks every 500.
The abscissa is labelled "True strain" and spans 0 to 0.8 with major ticks every 0.2.
The tested material is identified inside the panel by the printed label "Fe-28Mn-9Al-0.8C".

The red curve is identified by an arrowed annotation "True stress-true strain"; it rises from about 500 MPa at the lowest strains, crosses the 1500 MPa gridline near strain 0.6, peaks just above 1600 MPa between strain 0.6 and 0.7, and then drops steeply to about 1200 MPa.

The blue curve is identified by an arrowed annotation "Strain hardening rate"; it begins close to 2500 MPa at the lowest strain, drops steeply to a minimum of about 1550 MPa below strain 0.1, then rises to a broad local maximum just under 1900 MPa around strain 0.45-0.55 before decreasing again.
No numeric data labels, error bars, markers, legend box or scale bar are present in the panel; values can only be bracketed between gridlines.
The caption states the figure is a typical true stress-true strain curve of an MBIP steel showing very high strain-hardening rate.
The citing text states that the figure shows the true stress-true strain curve and the corresponding strain-hardening rate as a function of true strain for an MBIP steel.
The citing text asserts that the high work-hardening rate is a main characteristic of these low-density steels containing austenite, which distinguishes them mechanically from ferritic steels.

The citation describes the strain-hardening curves as evidence for ductility-enhancing mechanisms that raise the strain hardening rate during deformation, while stating that part of the strength derives from alloying and kappa-carbides (printed as j-carbides in the text).

Composition label "Fe-28Mn-9Al-0.8C" at lower right.

unreadable_items: No illegible text: all axis labels, tick numbers and arrowed annotations are readable. Exact peak values of both curves are not printed, so they can only be bracketed between the 1500 and 2000 MPa gridlines and between the 0.4 and 0.6 strain ticks.
